title: Treta Ke Thakur Temple Ayodhya - The Sacred Temple of Shri Ram’s Treta Yuga Avatar
content:
Treta Ke Thakur Temple Ayodhya

Treta Ke Thakur Temple is one of Ayodhya’s most revered and ancient temples, believed to mark the site where Lord Rama performed the Ashwamedha Yajna after returning to Ayodhya. This holy shrine stands as a timeless reminder of Treta Yuga and the glorious days of Lord Rama’s reign. Nestled near Naya Ghat on the banks of the Saryu River, the temple attracts thousands of devotees every year who seek blessings, peace, and a deeper connection with Ramayana history.

History & Mythological Significance

Treta Ke Thakur Temple is said to have been established by Vikramaditya during the ancient era and later renovated by various kings over centuries. According to legend, this is the spot where:

  • Lord Rama performed the Ashwamedha Yajna
  • Saints and sages gathered to witness the divine ritual
  • The divine presence of Lord Rama in Treta Yuga is still felt today

The current structure dates back to the 17th century and was renovated again in the 18th century by the rulers of the region. The temple houses beautifully carved idols of:

  • Lord Rama
  • Goddess Sita
  • Lakshmana
  • Bharat
  • Shatrughna
  • Hanuman Ji

All idols are carved from a single piece of black stone, making them incredibly unique and historically significant.

Architecture & Temple Beauty

Treta Ke Thakur Temple showcases simple yet powerful architectural elements:

  • Carved stone pillars
  • Large sanctum with ancient black-stone idols
  • Elevated structure reached by broad steps
  • Frescoes and carvings reflecting Ramayana episodes
  • Peaceful courtyard perfect for meditation
  • The temple’s antique charm and divine energy transport visitors back to the age of the Ramayana.

Why Visit Treta Ke Thakur?

1. Deep Ramayana Connection: This is believed to be one of the exact locations where Lord Rama lived and performed sacred rituals.

2. Rare Black-Stone Idols: The ancient idols of the entire Ram Parivar are carved from a single stone.

3. Open Only on Special Occasions: The temple opens to the public once a year on Ekadashi of Kartik month, making it extremely special.

4. Peaceful Riverside Location: Located close to Saryu Ghat, it offers a serene environment for devotees.

Location

  • Near Naya Ghat, Ayodhya
  • Walking distance from Ram Ki Paidi and Saryu River
  • Close to Ram Mandir, Hanuman Garhi, and Nageshwarnath Temple

Temple Timings

Treta Ke Thakur Temple generally remains closed throughout the year except on:

  • Kartik Shukla Ekadashi (one day annually)
  • On this day, thousands of devotees visit for darshan and special rituals.
  • On other days, the temple can only be viewed from the outside.

Best Time to Visit

  • Kartik Month (October-November) for darshan
  • Early morning or evening for photography at Naya Ghat

Nearby Attractions

  • Saryu River & Ram Ki Paidi
  • Ram Mandir (Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple)
  • Hanuman Garhi
  • Kanak Bhawan
  • Dashrath Mahal
  • Nageshwarnath Temple
  • Guptar Ghat

Festivals & Rituals

  • On Kartik Ekadashi, the temple comes alive with:
  • Beautiful decorations
  • Special aarti
  • Ramayana chanting
  • Thousands of devotees offering prayers
  • This is the only day when all the idols are worshipped publicly.
excerpt: Treta Ke Thakur Temple is a rare and ancient Ayodhya shrine linked directly to Lord Rama’s Ashwamedha Yajna. The temple houses unique black-stone idols of the entire Ram Parivar and opens only once a year, making it a sacred and exclusive pilgrimage spot. A must-visit place for Ramayana lovers and spiritual travelers.
